newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU sets new import duties on Russian oil products.
newsitem.headline: EU sets new import duties on Russian oil products.

text.p: The European Union has set import duties on Russian oil products from January 1 this year, Commission officials said on Monday.

The change -- automatic under a new EU Generalised System of Preferences (GSP) scheme -- means that the duties on the concerned products are raised to 50 percent of the normal existing duties on such products from other countries. There were previously no import duties on those products from Russia.
"Next year they will have to pay full duties," a Commission official said. "It was expected...the new GSP scheme leads to this conclusion."

The duty was set at 1.75 percent for some middle distillates and fuel oil. The normal duty on those products is three percent. It was set at three percent on gasoline as the normal duty is six percent.

But imports of gas oil below 0.2 percent sulphur were not affected. "Gas oil (below 0.2 percent sulphur) is not concerned by this because there is a unilateral suspension of duties regarding gas oil since 1990 and that is still in place," the official said.
There is also no import duty on crude oil.
